title: Technical Product Manager, Platform
description:
OUR MISSION:

At Sunrise Robotics, we are dedicated to augmenting humanity through intelligent robotics. Our mission is to elevate the world of manufacturing by introducing intelligent, flexible robots that enhance human capabilities and existing machinery, ushering in the next era of production at higher quality, with less waste, and lower cost.

OUR VISION:

We see a future where every element of manufacturing, from design to assembly, is optimised with intelligent automation. Our vision is to integrate flexible robotic solutions, based on generic hardware and advanced software/AI capabilities, into manufacturing, particularly in small and medium-sized enterprises, to make automation economically viable and accessible, for all sizes of manufacturers. We are not just building robots; we are creating the strategically crucial components for autonomous, intelligent agents of the future.

THE ROLE:

Platform is the core part of what makes Sunrise succeed: the software that lets a robotic cell see, move and recover, and the simulation pipeline we use to build and test all of it. You will own it.

You will own what Platform builds and why: which problems it solves next, what done means, and when it lands. This is not a backlog administration job. The engineers you will work with have strong, well argued technical opinions. You need the robotics depth to argue back with evidence, to challenge an estimate credibly, and to judge when the elegant architecture is worth the time and when it is not. The same judgement runs toward the customer: what Platform builds becomes the capabilities that decide which processes we can automate and which markets we can enter, so every technical trade-off is also a customer value decision.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Own the Platform roadmap

- Run discovery and prioritisation: turn ideas from customers, engineers and leadership into evidenced, prioritised jobs to be done.

- Turn prioritised jobs to be done into initiatives: write the specs, set milestones the team can commit to, and sequence them against the Sunrise roadmap.

- In robot software the cost of change is the core problem: a wrong requirement costs months, not days. Work out how much specification each decision needs, and catch the expensive mistakes before anyone builds them.

Run delivery with engineering

- Run cycle planning for the pillar, name the outcome of each cycle, and check that the planned work adds up to that outcome.

- Track dates against milestones with each initiative's technical lead. When estimates and targets disagree, cut scope, add people or move the date, explicitly and early.

- Sign off that delivered work meets the requirements and the quality bar written in the spec.

Be the technical counterpart

- Work daily with team leads and senior engineers on real trade-offs: perception accuracy against cycle time, simulation fidelity against speed, ship now against build it properly.

- Challenge estimates and accept challenge back. Arguments here run on evidence, not seniority.

Carry the customer into the platform

- Our customers are high-mix manufacturers, and the people who matter most are operators and facility managers. Bring their reality into every prioritisation decision.

- Work with the deployment team so what Platform ships works on a customer's factory floor, not just in the lab.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED:

- A robotics engineering background. You have built and shipped robot software (perception, motion planning, manipulation or robotics simulation) as an engineer or technical lead. This is a must. The role cannot be done from product experience alone.

- Senior product experience. You have owned a technical product area with 10 or more engineers and carried it from problem to shipped, including the messy middle.

- Spec writing where the cost of change is high. Specs and requirements that engineers respect and that hold up months later.

- Estimation and delivery discipline. Milestones, estimates with stated risk, and h

title: QA Engineer
description:
US Based Salary: $72,000 - $82,000 DOE
About Us
Bonterra exists to propel every doer of good to their peak impact. We measure that impact against our vision to increase the giving rate as a percentage of GDP from 2% to 3% by 2033. We know that this goal is lofty, but we are confident that the right technology and expertise will strengthen trust in the sector, allowing the social good industry to accelerate growth and reach peak impact. Bonterra 's differentiated, end-to-end solutions collectively support a unique network of over 20,000 customers, including over 16,000 nonprofit organizations and over 50 percent of Fortune 100 companies. Learn more at bonterratech.com.
About the Role
Who You Are
Are you passionate about quality and driven to ship software that works reliably at scale? Do you reach for automation before you reach for a test script? Is your first instinct when a bug lands to write a test that would have caught it?
You're an automation-first QA Engineer who approaches testing as an engineering discipline. Automation isn't a goal you work toward - it's the default approach for repeatable validation. You understand when testing belongs at the UI, API, or integration level, and you build reliable, maintainable automation that provides fast and meaningful feedback to the development team.
Manual testing still has an important place, but you use it intentionally for exploratory testing, usability validation, and one-time scenarios where automation provides limited value. Everything repeatable should be automated.
You write test code with the same discipline you bring to production code: code reviews, refactoring, reusability, reliability, and maintainability. When an automated test fails, you investigate it rather than simply reporting it, working to determine whether the issue is in the product, test, environment, or data.
Bonterra is seeking a QA Engineer - Automation to join our Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) engineering team. ETO is one of Bonterra 's flagship products - a large-scale enterprise platform used by nonprofit organizations and public agencies to measure, manage, and improve program outcomes.
You'll work closely with Software Engineers, Product Management, and Customer Success to validate new features, expand automated coverage, improve test reliability, and ensure high-quality releases for clients who depend on ETO every day.
What You'll Do

• Build and maintain automated tests for new features, bug fixes, and regression scenarios, prioritizing repeatable validation over recurring manual execution.

• Own and evolve the automated test suite as a production-quality codebase, applying sound engineering practices such as reusable components, refactoring, code reviews, and reliable test design.

• Help shape the team's test strategy and architecture, selecting the appropriate level of testing - UI, API, or integration - based on risk, coverage, maintainability, and execution speed.

• Build API and integration tests to validate business logic beyond the UI, including request/response validation, authentication and authorization, error handling, and data integrity.

• Participate in design and code reviews with a testability lens, identifying requirements or technical designs that may be difficult to validate and advocating for solutions that make software easier to test.

• Investigate automated test failures and identify root causes, distinguishing between product defects, test defects, environmental issues, and test-data problems.

• Identify and eliminate flaky tests, improving the reliability and trustworthiness of the automated test suite rather than routinely ignoring or disabling unstable tests.

• Identify and close coverage gaps based on product risk, business requirements, and customer impact.

• Validate features, defects, and releases through functional, regression, integration, and exploratory testing, including scenarios based on real customer workflows.

Are you a Nurse Practitioner who thrives on connecting with patients and making a real difference in their health outcomes? Do you want to leave behind rigid, cookie-cutter systems and join a dynamic, patient-centered organization that values your creativity and clinical expertise? If you're passionate about improving outcomes at scale and energized by meaningful patient engagement, we want you on our team.

At Galileo, we're transforming healthcare by delivering personalized, comprehensive care to those who need it most - underserved patients and those with complex medical needs. We use technology, data, and operational rigor to drive outcomes, and we believe the clinicians doing this work are central to that mission. We're a digital-first medical group, and we're proud of the culture we've built: inclusive, collaborative, and deeply committed to health equity.

Galileo is looking for a culturally-competent Nurse Practitioner to join our Population Health team. In this role, you will use phone and video-based care to provide high-quality, comprehensive follow-up care to patients who are post-hospital discharge.

Here's what you'll do:

• Cover our care needs for our Transitions of Care program. 

• Day to day work includes telephonic outreach (“cold calls”) and scheduled video/phone visits for patients who have recently been hospitalized and discharged. 

• Visits focus on: Medication reconciliation, symptom screening, and ordering of any needed follow-up labs, medications or supplies. 

• You will also navigate conversations with patients to build trust, explain Galileo's care model and connect them to services.

• Coordinate care across settings - hospital and ED transitions, pharmacies, and community providers - to keep patients connected and moving forward.

• Collaborate with our nursing team

• Be accountable to individual performance targets while contributing to team-level population health goals

How We Work

Galileo is a 24/7 medical group that provides high-quality, comprehensive primary care as well as transition of care follow-up. We work in 4-hour shifts (mornings, afternoons, evenings, overnight on weekdays and weekends). At 24+ hours you will be considered full-time and benefits eligible. Providers are expected to work weekends on a monthly basis, specific schedule will be influenced by total hours committed and patient care demands.

We are currently looking for a Nurse Practitioner with an active license in CT who is available to work a minimum 24 hours/week.

Compensation

$75/hour (regular rate) and $85/hour (premium rate)

About You

You're a people person. You love connecting with others and have an innate ability to build rapport quickly - even on a cold call. Your curiosity and creativity come through in every patient conversation, and you're looking for an environment where those instincts are an asset, not an afterthought. You enjoy collaborating with RN and administrative colleagues. You are flexible to changing workflows and enjoy solving problems. You identify systems issues and offer suggestions for improvement.

We look for passionate clinicians

title: Business Analist ANPR Verkeersveiligheid (Freelance mogelijk)
description:
📋 Taken en verantwoordelijkheden
Presentatie
Dit programma is ingebed in de directie Politie Informatie en ICT, die instaat voor de voorbereiding van beleid en regels rond informatiebeheer en -verwerking, de ontwikkeling van het politie-informatieconcept, het bepalen van technische normen en standaarden en de implementatie van informatie- en communicatiesystemen.
Project
Automatische kentekenplaatherkenning (Automatic Number Plate Recognition, ANPR) maakt gebruik van intelligente camera’s die nummerplaten herkennen. De gescande nummerplaten worden vervolgens vergeleken met beschikbare gegevens, bijvoorbeeld over gestolen of geseinde voertuigen of voertuigen die al dan niet in bepaalde zones mogen rijden. Binnen deze context wordt ANPR ingezet voor verkeersveiligheid en gerechtelijke opdrachten.
Missie
Als business analist binnen het ANPR-domein ondersteun je analyses binnen het domein verkeer en vertaal je behoeften vanop het terrein naar concrete voorstellen voor de stabilisatie en modernisering van het ANPR-systeem. Daarbij werk je aan uiteenlopende initiatieven, zoals functionele uitbreidingen, software-upgrades, procesmodellering (as-is/to-be) en het heroriënteren van bestaande oplossingen en materiaal.
Je brengt initiatieven samen in een gestructureerde aanpak, met aandacht voor haalbaarheid, prioriteiten, timing, budget en afhankelijkheden. Je werkt nauw samen met interne stakeholders, waaronder kerngebruikers, IT-architecten, projectmanagers, gegevensexperten, analisten en software engineers, en stemt waar nodig af met externe partners. Dankzij je technisch inzicht neem je een adviserende en faciliterende rol op naar zowel management als operationele diensten. Je bouwt snel domeinkennis op en documenteert die zorgvuldig om kennisborging en overdracht te verzekeren.
Je kan vlot schakelen tussen verschillende onderwerpen en past je aan wisselende prioriteiten aan.
Taken en verantwoordelijkheden:

•
Hoofdtaken:

• Zorgen dat requirements en standaarden voor alle verkeersinitiatieven binnen het ANPR-programma duidelijk en volledig zijn uitgewerkt.

• Processen in kaart brengen en analyseren, inclusief as-is- en to-be-modellen.

• Taken, afhankelijkheden en risico’s identificeren en opvolgen.

• De voortgang rapporteren aan stakeholders, met aandacht voor status, problemen, bottlenecks, risico’s, mitigerende maatregelen en beslissingen in een decision log.

• Kwaliteitsbeheerplannen opzetten en onderhouden zodat resultaten voldoen aan de vereiste normen.

• Stakeholdermanagement opnemen en duurzame relaties uitbouwen met interne belanghebbenden, eindgebruikers en externe partners.

• Informatie en analyses op een gestructureerde manier documenteren voor rapportering, kennisborging en overdracht.

•
Neventaken:

• Bijdragen aan een toekomstvisie voor een stabiel ANPR-ecosysteem op lange termijn, rekening houdend met capaciteitsgroei, nieuwe technologieën en integraties met andere systemen.

• Nieuwe ontwikkelingen in ANPR-technologie en relevante wet- en regelgeving opvolgen en deze inzichten verwerken in analyses en adviezen.

• Input aanleveren voor DPIA’s, risico-analyses en gelijkaardige trajecten in samenwerking met gegevensbeschermingsexperten.

• Minstens vijf jaar hands-on ervaring in business analyse en/of het begeleiden van ICT-projecten.

• Aantoonbare ervaring in complexe IT-omgevingen binnen overheidsinstanties of de publieke sector.

• Ervaring met analysemethodologieën en tools, zoals bedrijfsprocesmodellering, requirements management en systemen voor projectopvolging.

• Bekendheid met MS Visio, Power BI, Jira, Confluence of vergelijkbare tools is een plus.

• Sterk analytisch vermogen en probleemoplossende vaardigheden, met oog voor detail én voor het bredere geheel.

Sick of commuting? Tired of “hybrid” jobs that are really “in office” jobs in disguise? If you’re more productive at home than in an office, and want to make that arrangement permanent, we may have the position you’re after.
At CarriersEdge , we’re focused on producing great quality products and happy customers. We don’t care about being the coolest company in town, having the most amazing office perks, or the hippest staff. If you’re interested in those things, you’ll hate us.
On the other hand, if you’re not looking for a social group and just want to do great work, then you may be exactly what we’re looking for. We don’t care where you work and we won’t be looking over your shoulder micromanaging you. You’ll have minimal meetings disrupting your week, and plenty of time to focus on doing the best job possible. We’re growing, but not so quickly that things are chaotic.
As part of that growth, we’ve got an opening for a Graphic Designer.
The ideal candidate has a solid foundation in the skills outlined below, is a self-learner with a great work ethic, and has a keen interest in communicating through visual design.
This isn’t a big company with layers of bureaucracy and committees for every decision. It’s also not an agency where you’ll get crushed by client demands and deadlines. • You like to understand the “why” behind any assignment, including the context of the end user, so that your design solutions will be effective for the intended audience

• You’re a creative generalist, comfortable delivering across media - from print and web to social and video - and you like to teach yourself new tools

title: Senior Product Manager, Fulfillment
description:
About Faire

Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town - we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours.

About this role

Fulfillment is one of Faire's top long-term strategic bets that fundamentally changes how both brands and retailers do business. You'll play an instrumental role in scaling Faire's fulfillment business from 1% to 20%+ of GMV, working across the full problem space of brand supply, retailer demand, and unit economics to build the products and operational foundations that make Faire the best way for brands to fulfill wholesale and the most flexible, valuable way for retailers to stock their stores.

The product problems you'll tackle are both digital and physical in nature, spanning marketplace dynamics, operational systems, and program economics. You'll partner cross-functionally and with senior fulfillment leads to drive end-to-end execution and strategy on key workstreams touching brands, retailers, and operations.

We're looking for a product manager with deep empathy for how our customers' businesses actually work, relentless execution in ambiguous 0→1 environments, and the instinct to always connect what they're building to why it matters for the broader business.

What you’ll do 

• Brand supply.  Build onboarding, sales enablement, and operational tooling that makes it easier and more compelling for brands to fulfill through Faire, with a deep understanding of what it actually takes for a brand to change how they operate.

We are looking for experienced Freight Agents to join our network as independent contractors. We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.
We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.
In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.
The Role
We are looking for product engineers to own product areas within Doit's AI Investing App.

This role is for builders who can understand users, define product direction, work with engineering and design, launch fast and keep improving after release.
What You'll Own

• Own product areas across insurance, payments, savings, investing, travel or other financial services.

• Define user problems, product scope, success metrics, roadmap and launch plans.

• Work with engineering, design, data, operations, compliance and business teams.

• Turn complex financial products into simple, usable customer journeys.

• Use data, feedback, research and production issues to improve product decisions.

• Launch features, monitor performance and drive iterations.

• Make trade-offs between speed, user experience, business impact, compliance and operational complexity.

What We're Looking For

• Experience as Product Engineer, Product Owner, founder, growth/product operator or similar role.

• Strong product sense and ability to simplify complex workflows.

• Able to work with engineers and designers to ship real products.

• Comfortable with metrics, user feedback, experiments and post-launch learning.

• Strong writing, prioritization and stakeholder management.

• High ownership and ability to drive work with limited guidance.

• Experience in fintech, insurance, payments, consumer apps or high-growth products is a strong advantage.

The Kind of Builder We Want

• Starts from user problems, not feature lists.

• Can make decisions with incomplete information.

• Knows how to ship quickly and learn after launch.

• Works well with engineering without hiding behind process.

• Honest about what changed because of their work versus wider team effort.

This Role Is Not For

• People who only write decks and do not drive execution.

• PMs who cannot work deeply with engineering.

• Candidates who need perfect data before making decisions.

• People who launch features and then stop caring.

• PMs who exaggerate business impact without understanding attribution.

Location
This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Australia . We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Australia .
Language
English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.
Interview Process
Our process is designed to move fast:
1. Online assessment or practical task
2. Role-specific interview
3. CEO / final round
For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Account Executive, Product Sales - Crypto
description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies-from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups-use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Stripe’s Crypto Product Sales team is helping businesses move value into, out of, and across crypto ecosystems. We work with fintechs, platforms, marketplaces, and crypto-native companies to accept stablecoin payments, send funds globally, and make it easier for users to move between fiat and crypto. Our current focus spans stablecoin payins and payouts, Crypto Onramp, and other digital asset funding flows.

If turning crypto into practical global financial infrastructure excites you… you’ll fit right in.

What you’ll do

As an Account Executive on the Crypto Product Sales team, you’ll grow adoption and revenue for Stripe’s crypto products and the financial infrastructure that powers them. You’ll collaborate with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and other GTM teams to develop deep product and industry knowledge, lead complex deals, and help build and execute our go-to-market strategy.

This is a high-autonomy sales role on a close-knit team. You can move comfortably between business, product, and technical conversations, build value in competitive situations, and bring structure to an evolving market. You’re equally effective with customers and internal partners, excited to develop deep expertise, and generous about sharing what you learn.

Responsibilities

• Own a revenue target and the end-to-end commercial motion for Stripe’s crypto products, from pipeline development and qualification through negotiation, close, and launch.

• Qualify customer business models, fund flows, target geographies, end-user journeys, and regulatory readiness.

• Develop a deep understanding of the competitive and partner landscape, and use it to sharpen Stripe’s positioning.

• Navigate stakeholders across internal Risk, Compliance, and Legal teams, as well as financial and technology partners, from early qualification through launch.

• Use early customer engagements to develop repeatable segmentation, qualification criteria, commercial models, and GTM playbooks.

• Bring structured market feedback to Product and Engineering as the product and market rapidly evolve.

• Bring curiosity, good judgment, and a sense of humor - we’re building the playbook as we go.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Requirements

• 5+ years of customer-facing experience in technology, fintech, crypto, payments, or financial infrastructure, with a track record of strong performance.

• Experience building trusted advisor relationships with senior business leaders.

• Proven ability to build strong collaborative working relationships with cross-functional business partners.

• Self-starter capable of operating independently to drive meaningful business results.

• Willingness to roll up your sleeves and build where there isn’t yet a playbook.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

• Ability to understand complex technical requirements and craft solutions that address the needs of multiple stakeholders.

• Proven experience leading complex negotiations involving bespoke commercial agreements.

• Thrives in a fast-paced environmen

Lifecycle Marketing Manager
Remote (minimum 4-hour overlap with US Eastern hours) | Marketing | Reports to: Director, Revenue Marketing
Time Doctor is hiring a Lifecycle Marketing Manager to own the marketing-led customer journey from the moment an account starts paying. You will decide who hears what, when, based on which behaviour, and toward which commercial outcome. Your job is to turn customer behaviour and usage signals into adoption, retention, expansion and reactivation revenue, and to run that engine AI-first, building agents and agentic workflows that do real work.
Who we are
Time Doctor is a workforce analytics platform that gives distributed teams the visibility they need to improve trust and performance. We serve remote, hybrid and outsourced organisations worldwide, with particular strength in BPO, healthcare and tech services. We are bootstrapped, profitable and fully remote, with team members across 30+ countries. We built a durable business on customer revenue rather than venture capital, and we are now focused on growing it.
The role
You will own the lifecycle marketing program for our paying customers: the 30/60/90 onboarding plays, ongoing customer communications, customer segmentation, and the expansion and retention plays that grow and keep the base. You design the journeys, brief the work, QA it and measure it, and you own the revenue outcome.
Three things define this seat.

• The number. Your primary measure is the qualified expansion and cross-sell opportunities Lifecycle generates and surfaces. Expansion revenue, net revenue retention and at-risk recovery sit right behind it, shared with CS, Sales and Product.

• The lane. You own orchestration and outcomes across the customer base, not every surface you touch. PMM owns the message, GTM Ops builds the scoring and routing, and Growth and CS co-define the signals with you. You make it all work together.

• The operating model. This is an AI-first role, and AI fluency is the job. The bar is that you can stand up an agent that does real work, not describe one. Accelerating Time Doctor 's AI-first operating model is an explicit expectation of the seat.

This is a systems role. You build repeatable, automated journeys rather than one-off campaigns, and you keep human ownership of segmentation logic, offer design, guardrails, final QA and the commercial call.
Who you are

• You treat a revenue number as yours, and you design every journey toward adoption, retention or expansion.

• You have high agency. When a journey underperforms, you find out why and fix it.

• You are commercially minded. You turn customer signals into revenue.

• You are analytical and cohort-fluent. You read behaviour and act on where customers stall or grow.

• You think in systems. You would rather build a repeatable, automated flow than run another one-off campaign.

• You work cleanly across Growth, CS, PMM and GTM Ops without needing to own their surfaces, and you turn ambiguous boundaries into working agreements.

• You build with AI. Agents and agentic workflows are how you get work done.

What you will own

• Onboarding and adoption. The marketing-led 30/60/90 program that gets new paying customers to first value, plus ongoing adoption of key capabilities and education, including driving traffic to TD Academy and running education webinars end to end. You own the day-0 handoff: the trigger and the data that enrol a new customer in the right journey.

• Segmentation and journey orchestration. Segmenting paying customers on profile, product usage, engagement, lifecycle stage, adoption state, expansion propensity and churn risk, then designing, building and QA-ing the journeys and triggers on top, so the right cohort gets the right play at the right moment.

If you want your work on shelves everywhere - and outsized ownership while you build - we'd love to meet you.

THE ROLE

Data at Confido feeds customer-facing reports, internal dashboards, and a lot of day-to-day decisions. Right now it lives in too many places and is owned by too many people. We're hiring a Data Engineering Manager to fix that and to build the team that keeps it fixed.

You'll manage our Senior Analytics Engineer to start, and you'll hire as the team grows. For the first stretch you'll write a good amount of code yourself. Later, more of your time will go to hiring, planning, and working with other teams.

What You'll Do

- Manage and develop the data team, starting with our Senior Analytics Engineer.

- Decide what the team works on and in what order, and explain those calls to the rest of the company.

- Make the big technical decisions on warehouse design, pipelines, orchestration, and tooling.

- Hire data engineers as we grow. You'll write the job descriptions, run the interviews, and onboard new hires.

- Set standards for modeling, testing, docs, monitoring, and on-call.

- Work with Engineering, Product, Ops, and Customer teams to agree on metric definitions and figure out what data they actually need.

- Be accountable when numbers are wrong or pipelines break, and put fixes in place so the same problems don't come back.

- Write SQL, build models, and review PRs, especially early on.

What We're Looking For

- 7+ years in data or analytics engineering, with at least 2 years managing engineers.

- You've built a data warehouse from an early or messy state before, and you've kept it running afterward.

- Strong SQL and data modeling skills. You've built and maintained ETL/ELT pipelines in production.

- Experience with Snowflake, dbt, Airflow, Dagster, or similar tools.

- You've hired engineers and helped them get better at their jobs.

- You can take a vague request like "we need better reporting," figure out what's really needed, and turn it into a plan.

- You're happy splitting your time between managing and building.

Success in This Role

A year in, people across Confido trust the data and know where to find it. There's one set of core models the whole company uses, pipelines break less often, and when they do break, someone notices before a customer does. The team is bigger than one person, and it has clear standards that new hires can pick up quickly.

description:
Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.

About the Role

As a Senior Infrastructure Engineer on the Compute & Storage Platform team in Toast, you will design, build, and operate the foundational distributed systems powering the Toast platform as the company expands into further international markets and broadens its product offerings to encompass retail shopping.

A day in the life (Responsibilities) 

You will bridge the gap between core infrastructure and cutting-edge product development-building low-latency state and storage systems, scalable compute clusters, and high-throughput streaming pipelines. Your work will directly enable Toast product delivery across our Product Development Life Cycle (PDLC). You will bridge the gap between core infrastructure and cutting-edge product development-building low-latency state and storage systems, scalable compute clusters, and high-throughput streaming pipelines. Your work will directly enable Toast product delivery across our Product Development Life Cycle (PDLC).

What you'll need to thrive (Requirements)

Core Infrastructure & Automation

• Cloud & Infrastructure as Code: Hands-on experience building and managing scalable cloud infrastructure on AWS using Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, CloudFormation, etc.).

• Software Development: Fluency in Python , Go , or a similar language for infrastructure automation, tooling, or backend development.

• Storage & Compute Operations

• Databases: Deep experience operating and tuning enterprise databases at scale. This should include at least one variety of relational database (such as Postgres, Oracle, or MySQL) and at least one type of nonrelational database (such as MongoDB, DynamoDB, Opensearch).

• Containerization: Experience working with containerized environments and orchestration tools (e.g., Docker, ECS, Kubernetes).

Systems Reliability & Observability

Solid understanding of Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) principles, including monitoring, alerting, health checks, and performance troubleshooting in high-traffic environments.

Toast’s commercial products run on a stack that ranges from guest and restaurant-facing Android tablets to backend microservices, guest- and restaurant-facing web apps, payment systems, event buses, and more. 

The Infrastructure Engineering group manages Toast's infrastructure via the AWS API, using configuration management tools like Terraform, Ansible, and internally developed clients using Python and Go. We rely heavily on Datadog and Splunk for monitoring and observability and on FireHydrant for alerting and incident response.

Infrastructure Engineering provides the products and services to support, deploy, and monitor our product suite, which uses a microservice architecture written using JVM and Node.js apps. AWS products are also in heavy usage, ranging from S3 to RDS, DynamoDB, ECS, Lambda, and many others. We have our own platform for user management, service discovery/elevations, and load balancing. We use Apache Spark for large scale data workloads including query and batch processing. The main Toast POS application is an Android application written in Java and Kotlin. For data synchronization between tablets and our cloud platform we operate RabbitMQ and Apache Pulsar clusters as well as direct tablet communication to the applications' RESTful and GraphQL APIs.

** This is a hybrid role requiring in-office presence two days per week ***
